title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is a case of an AI-edited photograph being published as a real image of real people. The edit replaced one identifiable student with a generated image of a different person and altered the appearance of two others. The failure happened in the production of promotional material, at the point where an edited asset entered campus banners without any check against the source photograph or the university's own rules.

Catching it would have taken a review step that compared the final banner to the original photograph and to Stanford's policy, which bans using AI to produce or change images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities or achievements. The original photograph had been posted online by the dining service, so the unaltered version was available. Stanford has said the change and the failure to disclose it broke its policy, and that it is adding training and improving review of materials with Residential and Dining Enterprises.

What is not established is who made the alteration, whether it was deliberate, and what consequences followed. The reports describe a policy breach that the university itself acknowledged, not a finding of intent.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
In 2024, a Stanford photographer took a picture of Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic human biology senior, with two other students at a Lunar New Year event. The dining service posted it online. Last week, when Stanford used the image on campus banners, Ramirez had been replaced by an image of a Black woman, and the other students were made to look thinner. Ramirez learned about it from a friend and said he was upset and frustrated.

Stanford said on Tuesday that it used artificial intelligence to alter the original image. The university said its policy bans using AI to produce or change images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said the change and the failure to disclose it broke that policy. Stanford is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to add training and improve review of materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
